assembly_instructions: 1. Bolt the 200 mm x 200 mm x 8 mm aluminum base plate to four 16 mm diameter rubber feet, then install the four 190 mm corner posts. 2. Fasten the rear connector panel and the four top rim rails to the posts; leave the top and both side covers removed as a service cutaway. 3. Install the rail screws, blower bracket screws, board screws, and power-supply screws so the frame, pneumatic modules, and electronics have visible mechanical attachment points. 4. Mount the intake HEPA filter, blower bracket, centrifugal blower, O2 mixer, proportional valve, flow sensor, patient HEPA filter, exhalation HEPA filter, and their pleated media faces to the base plate in the visible left-to-right pneumatic order. 5. Connect the rear intake grille to the intake HEPA filter, the intake filter to the blower inlet, the blower outlet to the mixer, the mixer to the proportional valve, the valve to the flow sensor and patient HEPA filter, and the patient filter to the 22 mm inspiratory front port. 6. Connect the rear O2 supply port to the mixer through the 6 mm oxygen tube. 7. Connect the front exhalation-return port through the return hose to the exhaust HEPA filter, then connect that filter to the rear exhaust port. 8. Install the STM32 controller board, motor driver board, power supply, terminal block, cooling fan, and wiring harnesses on rear standoffs. 9. Assemble the operator front panel as an exploded service door on four standoffs: fit the touchscreen, two alarm LEDs, alarm-silence button, power button, inspiratory port, exhalation port, labels, and panel screws, then connect the ribbon cable to the controller. 10. Verify from the open top and removed side walls that the complete air path, oxygen path, return path, electronics stack, and standoffs are visible before fitting any optional covers.

info.japanese_name: MakAir オープンソース人工呼吸器
info.summary: Emergency-grade, open-hardware ventilator designed by the Makers-For-Life collective during the COVID-19 pandemic. Targeted at hospital shortages in low-resource settings.
info.description: MakAir is an open-source emergency ventilator designed in spring 2020 by Makers For Life, a volunteer collective of French engineers, medical professionals, and makers responding to the COVID-19 ventilator shortage. It is a compact blower-based ventilator: a brushless blower draws ambient air through a HEPA filter, mixes it with optional supplemental oxygen in a passive mixer, meters it past a proportional pressure valve with in-line flow and pressure sensors, and delivers it through a disposable patient HEPA filter to the inspiratory patient port. A separate front exhalation-return port routes expired gas through an exhaust HEPA filter to the rear exhaust outlet. A touchscreen plus two alarm LEDs on the front panel drive the UI; the STM32-based controller, motor driver, and power supply ride on the rear of the base. The enclosure is about a 20 x 20 x 20 cm cube; CAD, firmware, and bill of materials are released under open licenses so hospitals can manufacture locally.
info.operator: Field-deployed by Makers-For-Life partners and hospital maker-programs in 2020-21
info.contractor: Makers For Life (volunteer French engineering/medical collective)
info.contract_value: Target about EUR 500 in parts versus EUR 20k+ for commercial ICU ventilators
info.status: Open-source design; reference device certified for emergency use in several jurisdictions during COVID-19

facts.label: Form factor
facts.value: Approximate 0.200 m x 0.200 m x 0.200 m cube enclosure; scene dimensions use metres.

facts.label: Base plate
facts.value: 0.200 m x 0.200 m x 0.008 m aluminum plate with four 0.016 m diameter rubber feet.

facts.label: Patient circuit ports
facts.value: Two nominal 22 mm front patient fittings are represented by 0.011 m radius inspiratory and exhalation ports.

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Brushless centrifugal blower, passive O2 mixer, proportional pressure valve, flow sensor, pressure tap, and separate exhaust return filter.

facts.label: Control electronics
facts.value: STM32 controller board, motor driver, power supply, terminal block, cooling fan, touchscreen, and ribbon cable are separately modelled.

facts.label: Filters
facts.value: Three HEPA elements are modelled with visible pleated media: room-air intake, patient inspiratory outlet, and exhalation exhaust return.

facts.label: Oxygen input
facts.value: Rear O2 port feeds a 0.006 m class tube into the passive mixer.

facts.label: Open hardware cost target
facts.value: MakAir publications described a target bill of materials of about EUR 500.

facts.label: Service cutaway
facts.value: Side walls and top cover are removed and the front panel is exploded 0.065 m forward for inspection.

facts.label: Frame members
facts.value: Four 0.190 m posts and four top rails define the removable 0.20 m cube enclosure without opaque side panels.

sources.title: Makers For Life - MakAir on GitHub

parts.name: Intake Filter Blue Media Face
parts.role: Visible blue filter media face that distinguishes the HEPA cartridge from a plain box.

parts.name: Intake HEPA Pleat 1
parts.role: Raised pleat rib on the intake HEPA media showing folded filter construction.

parts.name: Intake HEPA Pleat 2
parts.role: Raised pleat rib on the intake filter face used to convey replaceable HEPA media.

parts.name: Intake HEPA Pleat 3
parts.role: Raised pleat rib on the intake filter face that breaks up the cartridge block.

parts.name: Intake HEPA Pleat 4
parts.role: Raised pleat rib on the intake filter face marking the air-cleaning element.

parts.role: Raised metal saddle that bolts the blower to the base plate and leaves tube clearance underneath.

parts.name: Blower Bracket Rear Screw
parts.role: Rear screw head clamping the blower bracket to the base plate.

parts.role: Circular centrifugal blower housing that pressurizes the inspiratory gas stream.

parts.name: Brushless Blower Motor
parts.role: Brushless DC motor mounted above the blower impeller and driven by the motor driver board.

parts.name: Tangential Blower Outlet
parts.role: Tangential rectangular outlet that makes the blower read as a centrifugal scroll rather than a simple can.

parts.name: Tube - Intake Filter to Blower
parts.role: Short silicone tube carrying filtered room air from the HEPA cartridge into the blower inlet.

parts.name: Rear O2 Supply Port
parts.role: Rear oxygen inlet fitting where supplemental O2 from a cylinder or wall supply enters.

parts.name: Passive O2 Mixer Chamber
parts.role: Inline mixing chamber that blends blower air with optional supplemental oxygen before metering.

parts.name: Tube - Blower Outlet to Mixer
parts.role: Flexible tube carrying pressurized air from the blower outlet into the oxygen mixer.

parts.name: Tube - O2 Port to Mixer
parts.role: Small oxygen hose routing supplemental O2 from the rear port into the mixer side inlet.

parts.name: Proportional Pressure Valve
parts.role: Servo-controlled valve that meters inspiratory pressure and flow into the patient line.

parts.name: Tube - Mixer to Proportional Valve
parts.role: Short tube that carries blended gas from the mixer outlet into the proportional valve.

parts.name: Valve Servo Actuator Cap
parts.role: Small actuator housing above the valve body that drives the proportional metering element.

parts.name: Inspiratory Flow Sensor
parts.role: Inline flow sensor that reports inspiratory flow for tidal-volume calculation and closed-loop control.

parts.name: Pressure Sensor Tap Tube
parts.role: Small pneumatic tap that samples pressure from the valve outlet and routes it to the pressure sensor.

parts.name: Patient-Line Pressure Sensor
parts.role: MEMS pressure sensor module that feeds the pressure servo loop and over-pressure alarms.

parts.name: Patient Inspiratory HEPA Filter
parts.role: Disposable outlet HEPA filter that protects the inspiratory patient circuit and is swapped between patients.

parts.name: Patient Filter Blue Media Face
parts.role: Visible media face showing that the patient outlet component is a filter cartridge.

parts.name: Patient HEPA Pleat 1
parts.role: Raised pleat rib on the patient outlet HEPA filter media.

parts.name: Patient HEPA Pleat 2
parts.role: Raised pleat rib showing the folded patient filter element.

parts.name: Patient HEPA Pleat 3
parts.role: Raised pleat rib that distinguishes the inspiratory filter from a plain housing block.

parts.name: Patient HEPA Pleat 4
parts.role: Raised pleat rib completing the visible filter-media pattern.

parts.name: Tube - Flow Sensor to Patient Filter
parts.role: Short inspiratory hose from the flow sensor outlet to the patient HEPA filter.

parts.name: Tube - Patient Filter to Front Port
parts.role: Visible flexible outlet hose linking the internal patient HEPA filter to the exploded inspiratory front port.

parts.name: Exhalation Exhaust HEPA Filter
parts.role: Return-line HEPA filter that scrubs expired gas before it vents through the rear exhaust port.
